newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU in 'get-to-know-you' talks with Japan minister.
newsitem.headline: EU in 'get-to-know-you' talks with Japan minister.

text.p: Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato arrived in Belgium on Monday for "getting-to-know-you" talks with the European Commission, officials said.

Sato -- appointed head of Japan's powerful Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) on November 7 -- has not met senior EU officials since his appointment because he has been tied down by a domestic bribery scandal.

He missed a key World Trade Organisation meeting in Singapore in December because of a widening probe into allegations that six senior MITI officials accepted favours from an oil dealer suspected of massive tax evasion.
"This is really an opportunity for us to get to know the man," said a European Commission official. "It is not really a meeting where we intend thrashing out issues."
Sato is unlikely, however, to be given much grace before EU officials begin pressing Tokyo on a raft of issues ranging from reform of Japanese market access to bilateral trade.

European officials said EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan would raise WTO issues, bilateral relations, ties with ASEM (Asia-Europe Meeting forum) and international technology agreements with Sato during their meeting.
Sato will also meet Commissioner Hans van den Broek -- responsible for relations with Eastern Europe -- to discuss cooperation in aid and foreign policy.
Sato, who arrived in Brussels from Geneva, will also visit Germany and Britain for meetings with his counterparts during his European trip.
